title: Using gcc: warnings, files, libraries
summary: The options you'll type every day, a program in several files, and the tools that build big projects.

scheme: around assignment used as truth value
text: gcc builds code that has obvious bugs without a word, unless you ask.
- -Wall turns on the warnings for the usual mistakes, -Wextra a few more.
- Here = stores 100 instead of comparing (==): every score is "perfect".
- Build with warnings on, always, and read them like errors.
A program in several files: give gcc every .c file. It compiles each one, then links them.
- Forget one and the linker says: undefined reference to `mean'.

scheme: link the maths library (libm): sqrt, pow…
text: #include <math.h> only promises that sqrt exists. Its code is in a library you link with -l.
- Put -l options after your files: the linker reads left to right.

scheme: -g      debug info: line numbers for gdb
-Og     debug build: code follows your lines
-O2     release build: faster, harder to debug
report memory bugs as they happen
Cargo.toml      cargo          Rust, all in one
text: Typing gcc by hand is fine for a few files. Bigger projects describe the build once.
- make rebuilds only what changed. CMake and Meson write the build files, then make or Ninja (faster) does the work.
